# greek-core-vocab

A reusable pipeline: fetch [Perseus's Greek Vocabulary
Tool](https://www.perseus.tufts.edu/hopper/vocablist?lang=greek)
weighted-frequency word lists for every *Great Books of the Western
World* work that has a matching Greek text on Perseus, and combine them
into one master core-vocabulary frequency list.

**The output**, regenerated by `make all` and checked into this repo so
it's usable without re-running anything: `output/master_vocab.csv` (+ a
`.json` mirror). One row per distinct Greek headword, sorted by combined
weighted frequency, descending.

**Current state**: of 142 `great_books.tsv` rows, 100 matched (117
unique Perseus URNs, all fetched successfully) and 42 were skipped (see
below for why); `output/master_vocab.csv` has 34,484 distinct headwords.
Top of the list is exactly what you'd expect -- ὁ, καί, δέ, εἰμί, ὅς,
τις, οὗτος, αὐτός, μέν, οὐ -- the core Greek function words.

## Quick start

```sh
uv sync
make all        # work-list -> match -> fetch -> combine
```

`data/raw/*` (the fetched per-work vocabulary lists) and
`output/master_vocab.*` are checked into this repo, so a fresh clone
already has the current output without hitting the network. `make all`
is safe to re-run: `fetch` skips any URN already cached, so after
editing `aliases.yaml`/`overrides.yaml`/`great_books.tsv` a re-run only
redoes the cheap, local matching + combining, not the fetches.

## How it works

1. **`fetch_work_list.py`** scrapes Perseus's own vocablist page for its
   full catalog of selectable Greek works -> `data/perseus_works.json`
   (`{urn, author, title, edition}` per work).
2. **`great_books.tsv`** is the input list -- title/author/group/year/
   sequence-number rows, copied verbatim from the *Great Books of the
   Western World* table this repo was built from.
3. **`match_books.py`** resolves each `great_books.tsv` row to zero or
   more Perseus URNs -> `data/matches.yaml`. In order:
   - `overrides.yaml` (exact author+title, or every row by an author)
     for the two rows that needed a human judgment call -- see below.
   - `aliases.yaml` for title pairs that share no usable substring
     (different English rendering, transliteration vs. translation,
     Latin editorial title, etc.).
   - General matching otherwise: normalize both titles (lowercase, drop
     a leading "the"/"a"/"an", strip punctuation), and match on
     equality, word-level containment in either direction, or an exact
     match against one comma-separated component of the Perseus title
     (Perseus groups several works -- mostly Plato dialogues -- under
     one selectable, comma-joined title; this is what resolves e.g.
     `Cratylus`/`Theaetetus`/`Sophist`/`Statesman` onto their single
     shared URN without hardcoding it).
   - A row that still matches nothing gets `matched_urns: []` and a
     `skip_reason` -- always recorded, never silently dropped.
4. **`fetch_vocab.py`** fetches every *unique* matched URN's vocabulary
   (deduplication here is what stops e.g. Plato's ~25 matched dialogue
   rows, which resolve to under a dozen distinct URNs, or Hippocrates'
   17 rows, which all resolve to one, from being counted more than
   once) -> `data/raw/<urn>.xml`, with a fallback ladder (below) ->
   `data/fetch_manifest.json` recording what actually happened per URN.
5. **`combine.py`** parses every cached file, groups entries by raw
   headword (the "collapse identical forms" step), sums each group's
   `weightedFrequency` across every work it appears in, converts the
   beta-code headword to Unicode (`beta-code-py`), and writes
   `output/master_vocab.csv`/`.json`.

## Why some rows need special handling

**Plutarch.** `great_books.tsv` has one row, "The Lives of the Noble
Grecians and Romans" -- but Perseus has no single text by that name; it
lists each of Plutarch's ~50 individual biographies as its own
selectable work (translator: Bernadotte Perrin), plus his ~18
"Comparison of X and Y" essays and dozens of unrelated Moralia essays
(Latin titles, different translators). `overrides.yaml` expands this one
row to every Perrin-translated, non-"Comparison of ..." work -- the
Lives themselves, nothing else.

**Hippocrates.** `great_books.tsv` has 17 separate treatise titles (the
Oath, On Ancient Medicine, Aphorisms, ...); Perseus's Greek vocab tool
only offers two omnibus editions, with no per-treatise selection and no
literal title match for any of the 17. `overrides.yaml` points every one
of them at the single English-edition omnibus
(`Perseus:text:1999.01.0249`, ed. W. H. S. Jones), fetched and counted
**once**, not 17 times.

**Everything else that's skipped** is a real absence, not a matching
failure: Archimedes, Apollonius of Perga, and Nicomachus of Gerasa
aren't in Perseus's Greek catalog at all; most of Aristotle's *Organon*/
*Physics*/biological-psychological works likewise aren't; "Dialogues"
(Plato) and "The Oresteia" (Aeschylus) are category-header rows, not
individual texts; and the Latin `great_books.tsv` rows (Lucretius,
Virgil) simply have no Greek text to match against this Greek-only
catalog. `match_books.py`'s own printed summary lists every skip.

## The fetch fallback ladder

`output=xml&filt=100` (every word in a work, not just a percentile) is
unreliable for big/heavy texts, in more than one way, both observed
fetching this repo's own data: it 504s near-instantly for the Iliad on
some runs (looks like a cached negative response rather than a real
per-request timeout); and for one work (Aristophanes' *Peace*) it
reliably returns HTTP 200 with what starts as valid XML and then, mid-
document, turns into a raw Java stack trace (a server-side Hibernate
lazy-initialization exception hit while rendering one particular
lemma) -- `looks_valid()` actually parses every XML response with
`ElementTree` rather than sniffing for a few substrings, specifically
because a substring check let that broken response through once.
`output=table` at the same `filt=100` doesn't hit either failure mode
(same data, HTML instead of XML), and dropping to `filt=75`/`50` (still
XML) also reliably works. `fetch_vocab.py` tries, per URN, in order,
until one works: `xml,100` -> `table,100` -> `xml,75` -> `xml,50`.
Whichever succeeds is recorded per-URN in `data/fetch_manifest.json` --
check it if you want to know whether a given work's contribution is its
full vocabulary or a percentile subset. In this repo's own data: 114
works via `xml,100`, 2 via `table,100` (Herodotus's *Histories*;
Aristophanes' *Peace*), 1 via `xml,75` (Aristotle's *Athenian
Constitution*).

## Collapsing and combining

Perseus's own tool already aggregates by lemma within one work -- the
`headword` field is a beta-code lemma, not a raw inflected surface form.
It does not, however, fully disambiguate homographs (two distinct LSJ
senses can share one `headword` string, split apart only in that
entry's lexicon-query references) -- "for forms that are identical,
collapse them into one reading" is read here as: group by the raw
headword string, full stop, both within a single work and across every
matched work. Each group's `weightedFrequency` values are **summed**
across every work it appears in -- a word that's both locally frequent
in one work and used across many works ranks highest, which is the
direct reading of "combine into one master list of frequencies" and the
standard way to merge frequency lists.

## Output columns (`output/master_vocab.csv`)

| column | meaning |
|---|---|
| `headword_unicode` | the lemma in Unicode Greek |
| `headword_betacode` | the same lemma in Perseus's own beta-code (the actual join key) |
| `combined_weighted_frequency` | summed `weightedFrequency` across every matched work containing this headword |
| `works_count` | number of distinct fetched works (URNs) it appeared in |
| `short_definition` | Perseus's own short gloss (first non-empty one seen) |
| `source_urns` | semicolon-separated Perseus URN ids (short form) it was drawn from |

## Re-running / extending

- Add rows to `great_books.tsv` (same 5 tab-separated columns) and
  `make all` -- new titles are matched automatically; add an
  `aliases.yaml`/`overrides.yaml` entry only if a title needs one (the
  scripts' own module docstrings explain the schema of each).
- `make fetch REDO=1` re-fetches every matched URN, ignoring the cache
  (e.g. if Perseus's own data has since changed).
- `uv run python3 fetch_vocab.py --redo` does the same directly.
- Lint: `uv run ruff check .`.
